profile.headline: Information Security & Software Engineer
profile.summary:
I'm a Java programmer with 25+ years of experience. I’ve recently changed specialties to cybersecurity (aka ISSE).

Specialties: Java, being a Dad

positions.title: Software Engineer Manager/Tier 3 O&M Team Leader
positions.description: Supported a contract with the Federal Government. Led a team of three in deployment activities (Java, Windows, Linux, and database deployments).
positions.insights: Skills: Software Deployment · Database deployment · Information Security Management · Windows Server · Red Hat Linux

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
Programmed in Java
Lead a small team working on the USN's PBIS application.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
•	Worked on the One NALCOMIS (Naval Aviation Logistics Command Management Information System) project.
•	Enhanced the One NALCOMIS logistics program which supports C4ISR requirements and utilized Java, Web MVC Spring framework, Hibernate and EJB 3.1 stack.
•	Enhanced application by adding Drools rules, Dojo client side validations, and creating JSPs.
•	Analyzed current code base and made recommendations for implementing a transactional and roll back framework.
•	Worked in an Agile environment.
•	Implementing end-to-end development by utilizing JSPs, Spring MVC, Dojo, web services, Spring sessions, stateless session beans, and Hibernate.  
•	Environment: Java, EJB3, JavaScript, Dojo, WSDL, JSP, Spring, Hibernate, Drools, JSON, jBPM, PostgresSQL, Sybase, JBoss, Eclipse.

positions.description: Worked on the NTCSSOA/One NALCOMIS project for SPAWAR

Programmed in VB and Java.
Implemented digital signatures.

patents.title: Variable trust levels for authentication
patents.description: “A level of trust is determined based on a combination of scores for one or more successful authentications. Scores indicate relative degrees of reliability for authentications, so that differing authentication methods may correspond to different scores. The determined level of trust can then be used to allow or deny access to a resource, and can be used to specify the type of access that is allowed, if applicable.”
